page: Microsoft Azure D4ds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is provisioned with 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. Memory capacity totals 16.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM balance of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include an x86_64 architecture with 260 MB of L3 cache, alongside Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction set extensions for accelerated matrix and vector workloads. Local storage consists of a bundled 236 GB NVMe solid-state drive.

Benchmark results reveal strong single-threaded data compression, recording 31.43 GB/s in gzip throughput. Single-core performance sits in the middle tier, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1722.0 and a stress-ng score of 1945.69. Multi-threaded capacity is constrained by the two-core physical topology, yielding a Geekbench multi-core score of 3881.0 and multi-core stress-ng score of 3984.38. Memory bandwidth measures 36.7 GB/s for large uncached reads and 25.67 GB/s for writes, reflecting entry-to-mid baseline memory subsystem bandwidth.

The bundled high-speed NVMe storage provides low-latency ephemeral scratch space without requiring external disk attachments for temporary files. Balanced memory density makes the configuration cost-efficient for standard mid-tier services, though high-concurrency tasks encounter throughput limitations due to the 4-vCPU ceiling. Microsoft Azure D4ds_v6 is suited for web serving, microservices, lightweight databases, software development builds, and modest batch processing tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure D4ds_v6 is a general-purpose instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, backed by a 2-core Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 host includes 260 MB of L3 cache, Intel AMX, and AVX-512 vector extensions, paired with a bundled 236 GB local NVMe SSD for fast temporary storage. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate solid single-thread performance, highlighted by a strong 31.43 GB/s gzip compression result, while multi-core metrics reflect the 2-physical-core constraint. Static web throughput averages 7.73 GB/s, and database operations score moderately in PassMark testing. With its balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio and onboard NVMe drive, the instance functions effectively for web serving, containerized workloads, development environments, and small-scale caching layers.
